name: Gyeongju
tagline: The capital of the Silla kingdom for nearly a thousand years, a museum without walls of grassy royal tombs, a grotto Buddha, a great temple and lantern-lit ponds.
highlight: Bulguksa temple's stone stairways and wooden halls in the soft light of early morning.
shortDescription: The ancient Silla capital, with the UNESCO-listed Bulguksa temple and Seokguram Grotto, giant royal burial mounds, Cheomseongdae observatory and the night-lit Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond.
metaDescription: A Gyeongju travel guide: Bulguksa, Seokguram Grotto, the Daereungwon tombs, Cheomseongdae, Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond, Hwangnidan-gil, food, where to stay, how to get there and a two-day plan.
nearestAirport: Ulsan (USN) or Busan Gimhae (PUS), about 1 hour; Singyeongju KTX station
knownFor: Silla heritage, tombs, temples, UNESCO sites
goodFor: History, cycling, temples, photography, slow travel

image.alt: The stairs and entrance gate of Bulguksa temple with a flower bed and blue sky

intro: Gyeongju was the capital of the Silla kingdom, which unified most of the Korean peninsula in the 7th century and ruled for nearly a thousand years, until 935. At its height the city was one of the largest in the world, and it is now a small, low-rise city of about 250,000 people whose parks, hills and lanes still hold much of that heritage. It is often called a museum without walls.

The sights are outstanding. Bulguksa, a temple founded in the 8th century, and Seokguram Grotto, a granite cave holding a serene seated Buddha, are both UNESCO World Heritage sites. In the city centre, grassy burial mounds rise like green hills at Daereungwon, Cheomseongdae is a stone observatory from the 7th century, and Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond are lit up at night. Gyeongju's historic areas together are also on the World Heritage list.

Gyeongju is easy to see at a gentle pace. Distances are short, cycling between sights is a pleasure, and the Hwangnidan-gil district is full of cafés in restored hanok. The city is about two hours from Seoul by KTX and 30 minutes from Busan, and two days is a good visit, ideally with a night in town to see the lit-up ponds.

whyVisit.intro: Gyeongju is Korea's best window into its ancient past, and a relaxing place to be.

points.title: A great temple and a grotto
points.text: Bulguksa and Seokguram are masterpieces of Buddhist art.

points.title: Royal tombs
points.text: Grassy mounds in the middle of the city.

points.title: Silla heritage
points.text: An observatory, palace ponds and museums.

points.title: Slow and walkable
points.text: A low-rise city that suits cycling.

attractionsIntro: Most sights are in or near the city centre, with Bulguksa and Seokguram on the hills to the east.

attractions.name: Bulguksa Temple

image.file: File:Bulguksa temple entrance gate stairs flower bed and blue sky in Gyeongju South Korea.jpg
image.alt: The entrance stairs and gate of Bulguksa temple

attractions.text: A temple founded in the 8th century, with stone bridges and stairways, wooden halls painted in bright colours, and two famed stone pagodas.
attractions.tip: Go early or late to avoid tour groups.

attractions.name: Seokguram Grotto

image.alt: The seated stone Buddha in Seokguram Grotto

attractions.text: A granite grotto on Mount Toham holding a large seated Buddha facing the sunrise over the sea. Photography inside is not allowed.
attractions.tip: Take the bus or a taxi from Bulguksa.

attractions.name: Cheomseongdae Observatory

image.file: File:Cheomseongdae Observatory under blue sky in Gyeongju South Korea.jpg
image.alt: The stone bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae observatory under a blue sky

attractions.text: A stone tower from the 7th century, often described as the oldest surviving observatory in East Asia, in a park of flowers.
attractions.tip: Visit in spring for rapeseed and cosmos blooms.

attractions.name: Daereungwon Tomb Complex

image.file: File:Trees surrounded by grassy tumuli at sunset in Daereungwon Tomb Complex of Gyeongju in South Korea.jpg
image.alt: Grassy tumuli and trees at sunset in the Daereungwon Tomb Complex

attractions.text: A park of large grassy burial mounds of Silla kings and nobles, including Cheonmachong, whose tomb can be entered and holds replicas of finds.

attractions.name: Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond

image.file: File:Water reflection of Donggung Palace in Wolji Pond at blue hour in Gyeongju South Korea.jpg
image.alt: Donggung Palace pavilions reflected in Wolji Pond at blue hour

attractions.text: The site of a Silla royal pleasure garden, with reconstructed pavilions around a pond, beautiful when lit up after dark.
attractions.tip: Come at dusk for the lights.

attractions.name: Gyeongju National Museum
attractions.text: A museum with Silla gold crowns, bells and treasures excavated from the tombs.

thingsToDoIntro: Gyeongju is a place to wander and cycle.

thingsToDo.title: Cycle among the tombs
thingsToDo.text: Rent a bicycle and ride between the parks and sights.
thingsToDo.tip: Electric bikes help on the hills.

thingsToDo.title: Stay in a hanok
thingsToDo.text: Sleep in a traditional house in the historic district.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Hwangnidan-gil
thingsToDo.text: Cafés, shops and restaurants in old houses.

thingsToDo.title: Take a templestay
thingsToDo.text: Spend a night in a temple for tea and meditation.

thingsToDo.title: Visit Yangdong Village
thingsToDo.text: A UNESCO-listed clan village of Joseon-era houses.

foodIntro: Gyeongju's food is simple, with local specialities like bread and rice dishes.

foods.name: Gyeongju bread (Gyeongju-bbang)
foods.text: A small pastry filled with sweet red bean paste, the city's best-known snack.

foods.name: Chalboribbang
foods.text: A soft barley bread with red bean filling.

foods.name: Ssambap
foods.text: Rice with vegetables and dishes, wrapped in leaves.

foods.name: Gyo-dong tea and beopju
foods.text: Traditional tea and a local rice wine.

accommodation.intro: Stay in the centre for the sights and the night lights.

areas.name: Hwangnam and Hwangnidan-gil
areas.text: Guesthouses and hanok stays near the tombs.

areas.name: Bomun Lake Resort
areas.text: Hotels by a lake, a short ride from the centre.

areas.name: Near Bulguksa
areas.text: Guesthouses on the road to the temple.

gettingThere.intro: Gyeongju has a KTX station outside the city.

options.text: About two hours to Singyeongju station, then a bus or taxi of about 20 minutes to the centre.
About an hour by intercity bus, or about 30 minutes by KTX to Singyeongju.
Buses from Seoul take around four hours.

gettingAround.intro: The centre is flat, so bikes and buses work well.

options.text: Rent one near the station or Hwangnidan-gil.
Cover Bulguksa and the main sights.

bestTime.headline: April and October
bestTime.summary: Gyeongju has mild springs and autumns, hot summers and cold winters.

seasons.text: Cherry blossom around Bomun Lake in early April.

bestTime.avoid: The peak of summer and long holiday weekends.

itinerary.title: Two days in Gyeongju
itinerary.intro: The hills and temple on the first day, and the city's tombs and lights on the second.

days.title: The city of tombs
days.evening: Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond at night.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you see Gyeongju well.
tips: Stay overnight to see the sights lit up.
Rent a bicycle for the central sights.
Check the bus times to Seokguram.
Combine a combination ticket for the central sights.
Wear comfortable shoes for the hills.
Try the local bread as a snack.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Gyeongju?
faq.a: Two days is ideal. A long day trip from Busan is possible.
Yes. It is one of Korea's best historic places, with UNESCO sites.

faq.q: How do I get there from Seoul?
faq.a: KTX to Singyeongju in about two hours, then a bus or taxi.

faq.q: Can I take photos in Seokguram?
faq.a: Not inside the grotto, but you can outside.
No. Bikes, buses and taxis are enough.
Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond are lit each evening.
